newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb kills one, wounds 10 in Algeria - report.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills one, wounds 10 in Algeria - report.

text.p: A bomb exploded by a cafeteria in central Oued el Alleug near the garrison town of Blida, killing one person and wounding about 10 people, an Algerian newspaper said on Thursday.

The bomb, hidden in a motorcycle, went off on Tuesday more than an hour after the break of the Moslem fast during the month of Ramadan in the town 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, El Watan daily said.
The bomb attack took place just hours after gunmen, said by the government to be Moslem fundamentalists, killed top trade union leader Abdelhak Benhamouda, in central Algiers.
The same day, a booby-trapped parcel exploded in downtown Blida, killing one person and wounding 17, Algerian security forces announced earlier.
The two bombs were in addition to seven bombings and massacres in Algiers and surrounding towns and hamlets during the first 19 days of Ramadan.
At least 178 people have died in this period. Algerian newspapers have put the figure at up to 250.
Algeria's ruthless Armed Islamic Group (GIA) warned it would step its attacks during Ramadan.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
